title_clean: The Exposition of the Elements — Dhātuvibhaṅga Sutta (MN 140) cont.
description_short: Bhante Bodhidhamma continues exploring the Buddha's profound discourse to Pukkasati on wisdom, truth, relinquishment and peace, concluding with Pukkasati's attainment of non-returner status.
description_long:
In this continuation of the Dhātuvibhaṅga Sutta (MN 140), Bhante Bodhidhamma explores the Buddha's profound teaching to the former king Pukkasati on the four foundations: not neglecting wisdom, preserving truth, cultivating relinquishment, and training in peace. The discourse reveals how through understanding the six elements and dependent origination, one reaches a state of purified equanimity—compared to refined gold—that enables entry into the formless jhānas (arūpajhāna).

The Buddha explains how a fully liberated being relates to feelings without attachment, remaining 'cool' even when experiencing bodily pain or approaching death. Like an oil lamp extinguishing when fuel is exhausted, the arahant experiences complete liberation upon the dissolution of the body. The talk explores the elimination of all conceiving (maññanā)—thoughts of 'I am,' 'I shall be'—which the Buddha describes as disease, tumor, and dart born from ignorance.

The touching conclusion reveals Pukkasati's sudden recognition of the Buddha, his request for ordination, and his tragic death by a stray cow while seeking requisites. However, the Buddha confirms that Pukkasati attained the state of non-returner (anāgāmi) during their conversation and was reborn in the Pure Abodes where he will achieve final Nibbāna without returning to this world.
